1: The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Ordinary third-person says and has replace obsolete forms; the perfect preparation and consecration remain. The repeated disappear, names, army of heaven, openly, the singular lamp, repeated near and day clauses, appointed mighty, third-person He pouring blood and flesh, and completion and haste are retained. No explanatory worship-versus-social-violence reading is inserted at 1:9.

Ordinary address uses you and verbs use comes, says and has. Ashkelon will disappear makes the shared future explicit; waterless wasteland and a wasteland express the ruined place naturally at 2:13 and 2:15. The passing flower, seek repetitions, answer these things, possibility of shelter, Cretans/Crete, has visited, away from the sons of Judah, Damascus, distinct Lord of powers/Almighty, islands, Ethiopians, chameleons, hedgehogs and cedar are retained.

3: The newer Bespoke Saints English (1).pdf governs, with accepted Genesis 1–11 as the English benchmark. It supersedes the older Founding Style Guide where their pronoun rules conflict: Thou/Thee/Thy/Thine address God directly; ordinary address uses you/your.

Ordinary address to the city uses you/your; third-person reporting uses says and has. Removed remains past while has redeemed makes the perfect explicit at 3:15. Conspicuous and redeemed dove-city, Arabian wolves, spirit bearers, the unusual exaction/strife clauses, number changes in 3:7, tongue for its generation and one yoke, repeated daughter Jerusalem, renew in His love and the feast in 3:17, the crushed and Alas, and the they/you distinction at 3:20 remain. The remnant clause at 3:13 still continues 3:12.
